questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Suriname?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Suriname on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Suriname article.

questions.proof: There are border disputes with French Guiana and Guyana all to the south of the country.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Suriname on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Suriname on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Suriname?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Suriname article.

questions.proof: Paramaribo is the capital city, in which resides almost half of the country's population.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Paramaribo?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Suriname is Paramaribo.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Suriname about 163,270 square kilometres; Dominica about 751 square kilometres; Saint Lucia about 617 square kilometres; Grenada about 349 square kilometres.
